title: When Leak Outruns Lymph
endLine: Edema forms when filtration outruns what lymph can carry.

scenes.tts: Small vessels leak a little all along their length, and plasma protein only slows the leak. Albumin supplies most of that pull. Yet adults born with almost none usually swell only mildly. What protects them?
scenes.narration: Small vessels leak a little all along their length, and plasma protein only slows the leak. Albumin supplies most of that pull. Yet adults born with almost none usually swell only mildly. What protects them?
scenes.visual: Continue the first film's world and colour map without a reset, rearranged (16:9). COLOUR BY CONCEPT, as before: blood pale RED with drifting dots flowing left to right; plasma protein (albumin) GOLD dots; the push WHITE arrows; the hold-back GOLD arrows; water and filtrate pale BLUE drops; glycocalyx a GREEN mat lining the tube. NEW in this film: lymph vessels and lymph node PURPLE. LAYOUT, kept all film: TOP 30%: the same capillary tube across about 85% of the frame width, 'arterial end' at left, 'venous end' at right, BLUE drops seeping out along its WHOLE length. MIDDLE: a dark band labelled 'tissue' whose thickness shows how much fluid it holds (it swells and shrinks). BOTTOM: a PURPLE blind-ended lymph vessel lying along the bottom of the tissue, closed at its left end, running right into a PURPLE oval labelled 'lymph node', then on to an arrow off the right edge labelled 'to neck veins'. RIGHT EDGE: two vertical bars, schematic with no numbers, labelled 'leak' (BLUE) and 'drain' (PURPLE). Link-back motion during the first sentence: BLUE drops seep out all along the tube while small GOLD arrows point back in, too weak to stop them. On 'Albumin supplies most', the GOLD dots in the tube glow. On 'born with almost none', most GOLD dots fade out of the tube (label 'almost no albumin'), the GOLD arrows shrink, and BLUE drops leak faster; the 'leak' bar rises. But the tissue band puffs up only slightly. On the question, white text across the top: 'What protects them?'

Title 'When Leak Outruns Lymph' fades in across the top for 2 s while the question text fades out. The GOLD dots return to the tube (normal albumin from here until s10); the tissue band returns to its resting thickness. BLUE drops keep seeping out along the tube.

scenes.tts: Start with where the leak goes. Filtered fluid enters blind-ended lymph vessels. Their overlapping cells leave flap-like openings between them, which let fluid in, not out.
scenes.narration: Start with where the leak goes. Filtered fluid enters blind-ended lymph vessels. Their overlapping cells leave flap-like openings between them, which let fluid in, not out.
scenes.visual: BLUE drops in the tissue drift down to the PURPLE vessel. On 'blind-ended', the closed left end of the PURPLE vessel pulses, label 'blind end'. Camera pushes in on a short stretch of its wall: overlapping PURPLE cells with small flaps between them, label 'flaps'. On 'let fluid in', a flap swings inward and BLUE drops pass into the vessel; on 'not out', drops inside push the flap shut and none escape. Pull back to the world.

scenes.tts: Bigger lymph vessels have valves. Each segment between two valves, a lymphangion, contracts as a pump. Squeezing from nearby muscle and from breathing also pushes lymph along.
scenes.narration: Bigger lymph vessels have valves. Each segment between two valves, a lymphangion, contracts as a pump. Squeezing from nearby muscle and from breathing also pushes lymph along.
scenes.visual: Further right, the PURPLE vessel widens and shows a row of small valve leaflets. On 'each segment between two valves', one segment is outlined and labelled 'lymphangion'; on 'contracts as a pump', it squeezes rhythmically and BLUE fluid inside steps rightward past the next valve, which closes behind it. On 'squeezing from nearby muscle', a pale band of muscle beside the vessel bulges and presses it; on 'breathing', a soft rhythmic pressure wave passes along the vessel. Lymph moves steadily toward the node; the PURPLE 'drain' bar rises to match the BLUE 'leak' bar.

scenes.tts: Recent reviews put an adult's daily filtration near eight liters. Roughly half is thought to rejoin the blood in lymph nodes. The rest enters the veins at the base of the neck.
scenes.narration: Recent reviews put an adult's daily filtration near eight liters. Roughly half is thought to rejoin the blood in lymph nodes. The rest enters the veins at the base of the neck.
scenes.visual: A small label by the tube: 'about 8 L a day (reviews)'. On 'rejoin the blood in lymph nodes', the PURPLE node glows and about half of the arriving BLUE fluid passes from it into a small RED vessel beside it; tag under the node 'estimate, mainly animal studies'. On 'base of the neck', the rest flows out along the PURPLE arrow off the right edge, label 'to neck veins'. The 'leak' and 'drain' bars stand level; the tissue band holds its resting thickness.

scenes.tts: Here is the one idea. Edema, swelling of the tissue, is filtration outrunning lymph. Fluid collects only when more leaves the capillaries than lymph carries away.
scenes.narration: Here is the one idea. Edema, swelling of the tissue, is filtration outrunning lymph. Fluid collects only when more leaves the capillaries than lymph carries away.
scenes.visual: The two bars move to the centre-right and grow larger. On 'filtration outrunning lymph', the BLUE 'leak' bar rises above the PURPLE 'drain' bar; the gap between their tops is shaded BLUE and labelled 'collects', and the tissue band visibly swells (label 'edema'). On 'more leaves the capillaries than lymph carries away', BLUE drops enter the tissue faster than they leave into the PURPLE vessel. Then the 'leak' bar eases back level with 'drain' and the tissue band shrinks to resting. Label at top: 'edema = leak beats drain'.

scenes.tts: So there are four ways to swell. Raise capillary pressure, as in heart failure, and the push grows. Lower plasma protein, and the hold-back shrinks.
scenes.narration: So there are four ways to swell. Raise capillary pressure, as in heart failure, and the push grows. Lower plasma protein, and the hold-back shrinks.
scenes.visual: A row of four small empty slots appears across the top, numbered 1 to 4. ROUTE 1 on 'raise capillary pressure': the WHITE push arrows along the tube grow longer, BLUE drops pour out faster, the 'leak' bar rises above 'drain' and the tissue band swells; slot 1 fills with 'pressure up'. Reset to resting. ROUTE 2 on 'lower plasma protein': GOLD dots thin out in the tube, the GOLD arrows shrink, BLUE drops leak faster, 'leak' beats 'drain', the tissue swells; slot 2 fills with 'protein down'. Reset to resting.

scenes.tts: Make the small vessels leaky, as in inflammation, and protein escapes, so the hold-back shrinks too. Or block the lymph, as in lymphedema, and drainage fails.
scenes.narration: Make the small vessels leaky, as in inflammation, and protein escapes, so the hold-back shrinks too. Or block the lymph, as in lymphedema, and drainage fails.
scenes.visual: ROUTE 3 on 'leaky': near the venous end of the tube, gaps open between lining cells; GOLD dots and BLUE drops escape through them into the tissue; the GOLD arrows shrink; 'leak' beats 'drain'; the tissue swells; slot 3 fills with 'leaky wall'. Reset to resting. ROUTE 4 on 'block the lymph': a dark X appears across the PURPLE vessel near the node; lymph flow stops, the PURPLE 'drain' bar falls toward zero while 'leak' stays normal; BLUE drops pile up in the tissue and it swells; slot 4 fills with 'drain blocked'. Reset to resting; the four filled slots stay at the top until s08.

scenes.tts: Now suppose filtration outruns lymph, and fluid starts to collect in the tissue. Which way does tissue pressure move, and what does that do to the push?
scenes.narration: Now suppose filtration outruns lymph, and fluid starts to collect in the tissue. Which way does tissue pressure move, and what does that do to the push?
scenes.visual: The four route slots fade. The 'leak' bar rises a little above 'drain' and the tissue band begins to swell. A small gauge appears in the tissue band, labelled 'tissue pressure', needle at its resting mark (no number). Question card at top in white: 'Tissue pressure: up or down?'

Predict pause. The question card stays. BLUE drops keep collecting slowly in the tissue; the tissue band keeps swelling slightly; the gauge needle trembles at its resting mark without moving off it. No other change.

scenes.tts: Tissue pressure rises, so the push shrinks. That is one safety factor. Faster filtration also rinses protein out of the tissue, which strengthens the hold-back. The third: lymph flow itself rises.
scenes.narration: Tissue pressure rises, so the push shrinks. That is one safety factor. Faster filtration also rinses protein out of the tissue, which strengthens the hold-back. The third: lymph flow itself rises.
scenes.visual: Question card dissolves. On 'rises', the gauge needle climbs; the WHITE push arrows along the tube shorten; label '1 tissue pressure up'. On 'rinses protein out', the few GOLD dots in the tissue band are carried off into the PURPLE vessel and the GOLD arrows in the tube lengthen a little; label '2 washout'. On 'lymph flow itself rises', the lymphangion pumps faster and the PURPLE 'drain' bar climbs; label '3 lymph up'. The 'leak' bar comes down to meet 'drain' and the tissue swelling stops growing. The three labels stay as a short list at right until s13.

scenes.tts: Back to albumin. Take a round teaching example. Halving albumin lifts the net outward pressure from one millimeter of mercury to nearly twelve. Washout brings it down to about eight.
scenes.narration: Back to albumin. Take a round teaching example. Halving albumin lifts the net outward pressure from 1 mmHg to nearly 12. Washout brings it down to about 8.
scenes.caption: Back to albumin. Take a round teaching example. Halving albumin lifts the net outward pressure from 1 mmHg to nearly 12. Washout brings it down to about 8.
scenes.visual: Tag 'teaching numbers' at bottom right. On 'halving albumin', GOLD dots in the tube drop to half (label 'albumin 4 to 2 g/dL'). A WHITE 'net out' meter appears beside the tube: its needle sits at 1, then on 'nearly twelve' swings to 11.8 (19 - 0.9 x (14 - 6)); BLUE drops pour out faster and the tissue swells. On 'washout', GOLD dots under the lining are rinsed away (label 'tissue-side protein 6 to 2') and the needle falls back to 8.2 (19 - 0.9 x (14 - 2)), label 'about 8'.

scenes.tts: Lower, but still large. So low protein is not harmless: filtration does rise. What holds the line is all three safety factors, acting together.
scenes.narration: Lower, but still large. So low protein is not harmless: filtration does rise. What holds the line is all three safety factors, acting together.
scenes.visual: The 'net out' meter holds at about 8, well above its old mark of 1. On 'filtration does rise', the 'leak' bar stands taller than at rest. On 'all three safety factors', the three listed labels at right ('1 tissue pressure up', '2 washout', '3 lymph up') light together: the gauge needle rises, GOLD in the tissue is carried away, the lymphangion pumps faster, and the 'drain' bar climbs to meet 'leak'. The tissue band stays only slightly swollen.

scenes.tts: In people born without albumin, globulins may partly stand in for it. That may be why their swelling is common but usually mild, and a few have none.
scenes.narration: In people born without albumin, globulins may partly stand in for it. That may be why their swelling is common but usually mild, and a few have none.
scenes.visual: The tube's GOLD albumin dots fade to almost none, as in the hook (label 'almost no albumin'); a sprinkling of TEAL dots in the tube, labelled 'globulins (may help)', adds a small inward arrow beside the weak GOLD ones. The three safety-factor labels stay lit. On 'usually mild', the tissue band settles only slightly swollen; on 'a few have none', it shrinks back to resting thickness for a moment, then returns to slightly swollen.

scenes.tts: So a steady leak is normal, and lymph carries it home. Swelling begins only when it beats the drain, and the tissue pushes back on three fronts.
scenes.narration: So a steady leak is normal, and lymph carries it home. Swelling begins only when it beats the drain, and the tissue pushes back on three fronts.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the full world with normal albumin restored. BLUE drops seep out all along the tube and drain into the PURPLE vessel at the same rate; 'leak' and 'drain' bars stand level. On 'beats the drain', the 'leak' bar edges above 'drain' and the tissue starts to swell; on 'three fronts', the gauge rises, GOLD is carried off and the lymph pumps faster, and the bars return to level.

End card over the dimmed but still moving world (BLUE drops seeping out along the tube and draining into the PURPLE lymph vessel, lymphangion pumping). Large white text, centred: 'Edema forms when filtration outruns what lymph can carry.'
